newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to reform health care system - Aparicio.
newsitem.headline: Spain to reform health care system - Aparicio.

text.p: MADRID, Feb 21 - Spanish Social Security Secretary Juan Carlos Aparecio said on Friday he hoped the country could reach an agreement to reform the health care system.
But he also added this reform is going to be more difficult than the one Spain had on pensions in 1995.
"In the health care system it would be desirable to reach an agreement similar (to the one we had on pensions), but this is going to be more difficult," Aparicio told Reuters in a interview.
Regional governments, currently providing health services to around 60 percent of citizens, have to be involved in reform talks, making the negotiations more difficult.
"..given that the 60 percent of the population is receiving health services from regional governments it would be necessary that the deal included them," Aparicio said.
He added the health care reform should go in the same direction as pensions -- "to adapt health expenditures to the expected growth in the economy in the coming years."
"The agreement is desirable and possible, but very complex," he said.
Aparicio said Spanish health expenditure was around five percent of gross domestic product.

Aparicio added that there are three guidelines for the reform -- to keep expenditure growth in line with the economic growth, to use both private and public resources and to improve efficiency in administration.
